facts.fact: Chetu of Upper Kuhl is a hill-council man whose valley has forty sacks left, all the regent's; he half-rises to speak for Pritam's grain at the Fair, then sits back when a woman says she paid four times the autumn price. He may reappear in ch31 as a reluctant signatory.

The officer of the forty lowers his spear because his own sister's house paid four times the autumn price for a bell-marked sack, as well as seeing Tej's sword belt on the grass. The 'And another' crowd chorus is cut.
Asha lays a page torn from Meera's count beside the book at the Fair; its dates match her own record of Varun's payments.
Rohan counted thirty-one graves and held the rope while the thirty-second was dug, so he states thirty-two to the assembly.

Meera writes her own name in the herald's book ('Meera of Kothi Shilak, called the Salt Fox') with the herald's pen; the herald adds 'Held pending the queen's judgement' beneath it. She says 'Law's a rope. Depends who ties it.'

In the Garh Neshar room Meera and Rohan have their second love scene; she keeps her left glove on and does not count anything afterwards. Rohan says 'The thaw is a long way off yet' as a plain sentence, not a promise, and the rope stays level.
